newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 29.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on November 29:

WASHINGTON - The D.C. financial control board and Mayor Marion Barry are moving forward with a top-to-bottom review of the city's police department by hiring a management consulting firm that will study crime-fighting in the District.
WASHINGTON - Despite the annual frenzy in stores the day after Thanksgiving, it is not actually the biggest shopping day of the year.
CHARLOTTE - In the high finance world of investment banking, where fortunes are made with top-end, billion-dollar deals, Erskine Bowles set his sights squarely on the middle.

TOKYO - A Japanese court has found a bank guilty of denying promotions to 12 female employees because of their gender, a landmark ruling in a country where women face discrimination in nearly every aspect of their lives.

FORT BLISS, Texas - With little public fanfare and scant Congressional scrutiny, the U.S. military's role in the nation's drug war has expanded as the Pentagon is increasingly drawn into domestic police missions.

RENIHUE, Chile - American Douglas Thompson, the founder of the Esprit clothing chain, bought a 600-acre ranch in a remote corner of Chile six years ago. He now wants to turn it into a national park, but his rain forest gift has aroused suspicions.
